articles.title: MCLAREN'S NEW LOGO LOOKS LIKE A LUXURY FASHION BRAND
articles.summary: McLaren has unveiled a refined brand identity that modernizes its wordmark while drawing inspiration from the signage of the McLaren family's original service station, balancing heritage with a more contemporary look. The redesign also retains the iconic Speedmark for its racing and golf divisions, reinforcing brand continuity while signaling a new chapter for the company.

articles.title: THE BOLD NEW APPLE MUSIC LOGO SIGNALS THE END OF MINIMALISM
articles.summary: Apple has quietly introduced a bold new Apple Music wordmark alongside the launch of Apple Music Hall in London, replacing its minimalist branding with a retro-inspired, lowercase logo that signals a shift toward a more expressive visual identity. The redesign reflects Apple's growing embrace of bolder, more playful aesthetics and could hint at the direction of its future design language.

articles.title: BRINGING EMOJI INTO THE NEXT ERA OF EXPRESSION
articles.summary: Noto 3D redraws emoji by hand rather than automating the jump into three dimensions, keeping expression readable at 18 pixels instead of chasing photorealism. Rotating the camera exposed legacy mistakes, including a poodle with three legs, and research showed that anatomical detail slows how fast people read emotion. An AI contrast audit flagged where darker skin tones vanish in dark mode across all 3,977 characters, and the library ships open source.

articles.title: PROPS ARE NOT A DESIGN SYSTEM
articles.summary: Inline styling — via Tailwind classes or style attributes — makes every component a one-off decision, breaking visual consistency, semantics, and maintainability. The proposed fix is defining styles once through named "variants" (complete, self-contained visual definitions) and "modifiers" (controlled variations like size), rather than overriding styles at the call site. Following this discipline across any UI kit naturally produces a real design system, turning scattered styling decisions into a reusable, consistent structure.

articles.title: DECISION PARALYSIS, LOST CONVICTION AND NO JUNIORS: WHAT BRAND CREATIVE LEADERS SAY AI IS EXPOSING
articles.summary: Brand Perspectives 2026, a MikeTeevee report drawing on in-house leaders at Wayfair, DoorDash, Intuit, O2, Canva, and Rivian, found that AI accelerated problems that predate it. Teams generating endless variations at near-zero cost now stall on choosing, while trimmed junior roles take the mid-level pipeline with them. Efficiency has not lightened the load: everyone reports working twice as hard, with handoffs still run off spreadsheets.

articles.title: PLEASE DON'T STRETCH YOUR APP FOR FOLDABLES
articles.summary: Foldable devices require apps to adapt to changing screen sizes, orientations, and postures with responsive layouts, multi-pane interfaces, and hinge-aware designs that preserve context and usability instead of simply stretching existing mobile UIs. By designing around available space rather than specific devices, teams can create experiences that work consistently across phones, foldables, tablets, and desktop-sized windows while following platform-specific layout conventions.

articles.title: ON MAKING ROOM FOR CRAFT
articles.summary: Reducing scope instead of quality means treating a complete, reliable user experience as non-negotiable while cutting optional features when time is limited. Teams should estimate and prioritize the full interaction—including loading states, errors, and edge cases—assign ownership for polishing core flows, and make deliberate trade-offs so products don't rely on last-minute fixes to feel complete.

articles.title: ORIGINALITY IS OVERRATED. ELABORATION IS THE THING
articles.summary: Research suggests that creative work delivers the strongest business results not through originality alone, but through elaboration—the careful refinement and execution that turn a good idea into a polished, effective campaign. As AI makes generating novel ideas easier, human value increasingly lies in the thousands of design decisions, craftsmanship, and attention to detail that set exceptional work apart from merely original work.

articles.title: EIGHT LESSONS FOR BRAND BUILDERS IN THE AGE OF AI
articles.summary: Forty-four hours of Brand Builders Summit 2026, across 48 speakers, circle one question: what makes a brand builder irreplaceable?

articles.title: JENNA ARTS ON WHY THE STUMBLING, SILLY, ORDINARY HUMAN IS THE ONLY ONE WORTH DRAWING
articles.summary: Illustrator Jenna Arts celebrates imperfection and everyday humanity, arguing that the authenticity, personality, and flaws of human-made art are what make it meaningful in an AI-driven world.
